t.E650.agn: In 1982 JECFA set a provisional maximum tolerable daily intake for zinc of 0.3–1 mg/kg body weight; in 2002 the SCF set a tolerable upper intake level for adults of 25 mg per day. In the EU its use is authorised only in chewing gum, at up to 1,000 mg/kg.
t.E650.body: Zinc is absorbed mainly from the first part of the small intestine (duodenum); its absorption is affected by substances in food such as phytate and soya protein. A protein called metallothionein plays a role in the body's zinc balance.
t.E650.eval: A zinc salt; in the EU authorised only in chewing gum (max. 1,000 mg/kg) as a flavour enhancer. Zinc is a mineral the body needs; the SCF set a tolerable upper intake for adults of 25 mg per day.
t.E650.prod: Produced chemically by reacting zinc oxide with acetic acid.
t.E650.regx.0: Only in chewing gum (category 05.3), max. 1,000 mg/kg.
t.E650.regx.1: Zinc: provisional maximum tolerable daily intake 0.3–1 mg/kg body weight.
t.E650.regx.2: SCF (2002): tolerable upper intake level for adults 25 mg/day (EFSA summary table).
t.E650.summary: Zinc acetate. Used as a flavour enhancer in chewing gum.
t.E650.what: A zinc salt used as a flavour enhancer in chewing gum. Zinc is a mineral the body needs.
